summary: Radar for 2026-10-20. Two things stand out. First, the Menopause Society Annual Meeting (Oct 20–24) opened today with two fresh women's-health GLP-1 results. Novo's post hoc REDEFINE 1 analysis reports an average 25% weight loss on CagriSema in 2,309 women at 68 weeks, versus 3% on placebo. A Mayo Clinic observational cohort links menopause hormone therapy to greater weight loss on semaglutide; the tirzepatide result was not statistically significant. These are the only Lane C (first explainer within 48 h) opportunities this week. Second, our strongest lane, gray-market "what's confirmed?", has new hooks. The FDA classified a nationwide Class II recall of Apothecary Pharma compounded tirzepatide on Oct 10, and USA Today covered it on Oct 19–20. A separate Houston compounding pharmacy drew 14 FDA inspection observations. There are FDA death reports involving illicit retatrutide, though FDA says it is not certain the drug caused them, plus an Australian liver-injury cluster, a rise in the Netherlands and a Bloomberg feature on Brazil's black market. That gives the two required Lane B long-forms. For Lane A search demand: Reuters (Oct 20) reports doctors and regulators flagging 'GLP-1 supplements', a cost-driven discontinuation study is in the news, and 'Wegovy pill vs shot' questions are rising. I checked: the 'online platform stops selling GLP-1s' story is from May 2026, not new. The orforglipron ACHIEVE-4 heart-safety result is about 3 weeks old and orforglipron underperforms for us. The semaglutide handgrip meta-analysis abstract couldn't be loaded, so the fact-checker needs to confirm it before use. Rejected: SEO-spam 'does tirzepatide cause breast cancer' and 'FDA adds new warning to Wegovy' pages, and law-firm NAION content.

candidates.topic: CagriSema in women: average 25% weight loss at 68 weeks in a post hoc REDEFINE 1 analysis (2,309 women; 3% on placebo), by menopause stage: 26.7% premenopausal, 24.8% perimenopausal, 23.1% postmenopausal. Presented at the Menopause Society Annual Meeting, Oct 20, 2026
candidates.angle: Lane C first explainer, new news first in the title: 'CagriSema in Women: What the New 25% Analysis Means'. Explain what CagriSema is (amylin analog cagrilintide plus semaglutide, a weekly injection). Explain why a post hoc subgroup is weaker evidence than the main REDEFINE 1 result (22.7% overall). Explain why weight loss looked similar across menopause stages. Status: investigational, not FDA-approved as of Oct 2026 (Novo, dated). Population: adults with obesity, or overweight with a weight-related condition, without diabetes. Avoid the 'Did X beat Y' frame, since there is no head-to-head trial. Mention common side effects (nausea and other stomach effects, mostly mild to moderate). Include the prescriber line.
candidates.why_now: Novo press release and CNBC/Reuters pickup this morning (Oct 20), with the conference running to Oct 24. Few creator explainers exist yet. It is the only fresh named-drug result that fits Lane C within 48 h, and it reaches women 45+, a core audience segment.

evidence.signal: Post hoc REDEFINE 1 analysis: 25% average weight loss in women at 68 weeks, presented at the Menopause Society meeting
Mainstream pickup: 2,309 women, 25% vs 3% on placebo, menopause-stage breakdown
Systematic review and meta-analysis of CagriSema vs semaglutide 2.4 mg, for context on the trial-level comparison

candidates.topic: Retatrutide online: what the FDA, Lilly and regulators have confirmed (Oct 2026). Not approved anywhere. FDA has received at least 2 death reports involving illicit retatrutide, with causation uncertain. Victoria (Australia) reported a liver-injury cluster. Lilly filed 6 lawsuits against sellers (Aug 12, 2026). The Netherlands reports rising use. Malaysia's health ministry issued a warning
candidates.angle: Lane B long-form 'Retatrutide Online: What the FDA and Lilly Have Confirmed', plus a 13:00 lead Short. Use a calm, dated attribution on every line. Quote Lilly CMO David Hyman's words exactly: 'not a medicine – it is entirely unverified, unapproved'. Say plainly that the FDA reports do not prove the drug caused the deaths. Contrast it with the real Phase 3 TRIUMPH trials. Never name sellers or explain how to buy. Point viewers to a prescriber about approved options or clinical trials.
candidates.why_now: Futurism (Oct 17), NL Times (Oct 19) and Stocktwits (Oct 20) coverage, plus heavy SEO search pages for 'retatrutide approval status'. This is our best Short lane (median 103.5, 1.9×) and has never been tested as a long-form, which is exactly Exp B.

evidence.signal: FDA has received at least 2 death reports linked to illicit retatrutide; causation not established
Lilly sues 6 companies selling retatrutide knockoffs
Liver-injury cluster in Victoria linked to unregulated 'retatrutide'
Lilly statement on the lawsuits and CMO quote

candidates.topic: Compounded tirzepatide recalled nationwide: Apothecary Pharma vials (lots AP-202622 to AP-202644) recalled for 'lack of assurance of sterility' (started Sept 24; FDA Class II, Oct 10). A Houston compounding pharmacy drew 14 FDA inspection observations, including research-grade ingredients
candidates.angle: Lane B long-form or 13:00 Short: 'Compounded Tirzepatide Recall: What the FDA Has Confirmed'. Explain what Class II means, quoting FDA's wording exactly. Explain how compounded products differ from FDA-approved tirzepatide, and why 'research-grade' ingredients matter. Tell viewers to check with their pharmacist or prescriber if they have questions about their medicine. No brand hashtags (#Mounjaro or #Zepbound), no emoji, no stopping or switching advice. Never name where to buy.
candidates.why_now: USA Today, Democrat and Chronicle and qz.com covered it Oct 19–20, and Medical Daily reported the Houston inspection findings on Oct 19. Our compounded Short got 91 at 20:00. This also builds on the previous Chinese-ingredient-plant snapshot (LA Times picked it up Oct 19).

evidence.signal: Nationwide recall, Class II on Oct 10, affected lots listed
Houston pharmacy behind recalled vials drew 14 FDA observations
Black mould and bugs found at Chinese plants making GLP-1 compounding ingredients

candidates.topic: Semaglutide vs tirzepatide in menopause: hormone therapy linked to greater, sustained weight loss on semaglutide (about 2,400 women), while the tirzepatide result (about 1,500 women) was not statistically significant. Mayo Clinic retrospective cohort of women over 45 with BMI over 27, Menopause Society meeting, Oct 20, 2026
candidates.angle: Two-drug body-effect head-to-head (works on both YouTube and Instagram), as a 13:00 or 08:00 Short and a possible Lane C long-form 'Menopause and GLP-1: Does Hormone Therapy Change Results?'. Use 'linked to', not 'causes'. Quote the lead author's caveats exactly: 'too early to draw firm conclusions' and 'weight loss is not an indication for menopause hormone therapy'. Mention the earlier Mayo tirzepatide study (Lancet Obstet Gynaecol Womens Health, Feb 2026: 40 women on hormone therapy vs 80 not). Close with: talk to your doctor or prescriber; don't start or change hormones on your own.
candidates.why_now: Medical Xpress published it this morning, and the topic overlaps with today's CagriSema-in-women news from the same meeting. Menopause plus GLP-1 is a steady search theme for women 45+ in the US/UK. Thin creator coverage of the new semaglutide-vs-tirzepatide contrast.

evidence.signal: Retrospective cohort, Menopause Society 2026: hormone therapy linked to greater semaglutide weight loss; tirzepatide not significant
40 women on hormone therapy vs 80 not; Lancet Obstet Gynaecol Womens Health

candidates.topic: Do 'GLP-1 supplements' work? Reuters (Oct 20) reports that doctors and regulators are raising flags as GLP-1 users turn to supplements, with TikTok driving the boom. The American College of Physicians has pressed the FDA for stronger supplement rules
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form 'Do GLP-1 Supplements Work? What the Evidence Says'. Explain the difference between a prescription GLP-1 medicine and a supplement labelled 'GLP-1'. Cover what actually supports your own GLP-1 (protein, fibre, eating order, movement), with honest effect sizes, and say clearly that none of them replace the medicine. No product names or links. Positive tone, no fear framing.
candidates.why_now: Reuters published two items today and Nutrition Insight one. This builds on the Bon Appétit test from the previous snapshot (seen twice). Search volume for 'GLP-1 supplement' is high, and the evergreen tail could last for months.

evidence.signal: As weight-loss drug users turn to dietary supplements, doctors and regulators raise flags
American College of Physicians presses the FDA for stronger supplement regulation
GLP-1-branded supplements on TikTok Shop with undisclosed affiliate selling

candidates.topic: Why do people stop semaglutide or tirzepatide? In a US national survey (J Manag Care Spec Pharm), the top reasons were cost (36.1%), side effects (33.3%), no insurance coverage (28.2%) and reaching a goal (26.1%). New: a copay-price study (VPM, Oct 19) and a real-world semaglutide persistence study (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 19)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form 'Why Do People Stop Tirzepatide or Semaglutide?'. Explain the reasons, then what helps people stay on track: managing common stomach side effects with their prescriber, protein and strength training, and asking about coverage or savings programmes. Briefly mention what SURMOUNT-4 showed about regain. Never advise stopping or switching; include 'don't stop or change your medicines on your own'.
keywords: what happens when you stop Mounjaro
candidates.predicted_peak: evergreen, refreshed over the next 7 days
candidates.why_now: The copay study and the DOM persistence paper came out on Oct 19. It fits the 'What happens when you stop' search question the playbook lists for Lane A, and builds on the stopping topic seen 6 times in earlier snapshots.

evidence.signal: Costs, side effects and reaching goals commonly drive discontinuation; 54.6% stopped within 6 months
Real-world semaglutide starting patterns, early discontinuation and 1-year persistence
Higher GLP-1 costs lead to lower adherence

candidates.topic: Wegovy pill vs Wegovy shot (oral vs injectable semaglutide for weight): how they compare and who shouldn't switch on their own. Yahoo Creators doctor explainer and Men's Journal 'switched to a daily pill' coverage, both Oct 20, 2026
candidates.angle: Lane A search-question long-form 'Wegovy Pill vs Wegovy Shot: What's the Difference?'. Cover daily vs weekly, the food and water rules for the pill, trial weight results each in its own population (no head-to-head unless the source has one; label indirect comparisons), and the same common side effects. Carries the 'don't switch on your own' line. Generic name first.
candidates.why_now: Several outlets ran pieces today, Amazon Pharmacy now offers the pill, and the 'pill vs shot' question has rising search intent. Note: semaglutide-only titles have underperformed for us, so the title must name both forms.

evidence.signal: Doctor explains how the Wegovy pill and shot compare, and who shouldn't switch
Wegovy users switched to a daily pill

candidates.topic: Does semaglutide reduce muscle strength? New systematic review and meta-analysis of handgrip strength after semaglutide (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 19, 2026), paired with the SURMOUNT-1 tirzepatide body-scan substudy
candidates.angle: Muscle as a question or outcome (99 and 130 views): a 08:00 Short 'Semaglutide vs tirzepatide: does strength drop as weight drops?'. Lean mass is not the same as strength; explain what the handgrip data show. Tips: protein (check first if you have kidney disease), start strength training gently. The fact-checker must pull the abstract first: it would not load during verification, so no direction of effect is claimed here.
candidates.why_now: Published yesterday, with no news pickup yet. Muscle loss is a top question from GLP-1 users, and strength data is a fresh angle beyond lean mass.

evidence.signal: Systematic review and meta-analysis of handgrip strength after semaglutide
Rapid review of protein intake plus resistance training across clinical populations
